note: Editors can add options here without changing code. Look options never change personality or difficulty.

options.label: Interrupts
options.description: Cuts in with Points of Information while you're still talking.

options.label: Demands evidence
options.description: Asks "Source?" whenever you make a claim.

options.label: Rapid stats
options.description: Throws quick, general numbers at you to sound certain.

options.label: Thought experiments
options.description: Answers with "Imagine..." hypotheticals.

options.label: Rhetorical questions
options.description: Asks questions that answer themselves.

options.label: Slippery slope
options.description: Warns where your idea "leads" if you keep going.

options.label: Emotional appeal
options.description: Tells short human stories to win hearts.

options.label: History appeal
options.description: Says "History shows..." to back its point.

options.label: Cites treaties
options.description: Refers to treaties and past UN resolutions in general terms.

options.label: Reframes the question
options.description: Changes what the question is about.

options.label: Turns your point around
options.description: Uses your own point against you.

options.label: Yes-or-no traps
options.description: Demands "Yes or no, delegate?" on tricky questions.

options.label: Pins down dodges
options.description: Won't let a dodge slide. Asks again, politely.

options.label: Procedural objections
options.description: Raises Points of Order on informal language.

options.label: Long answers
options.description: Talks long to eat time (still within word limits).

options.label: Changes the subject
options.description: Pivots to a topic where it is stronger.

options.label: Flattery, then attack
options.description: Compliments you first, then strikes.

options.label: Devil's advocate
options.description: Argues the opposite on purpose to test you.

options.label: Finds contradictions
options.description: Says "Earlier you said..." when you contradict yourself.

options.label: Analogies
options.description: Explains everything with comparisons.

options.label: Demands specifics
options.description: Asks "Which country? Which year?" when you're vague.

options.label: Quotes you back
options.description: Repeats your exact words back to you.

options.label: So what?
options.description: Asks "Why does that matter?"

options.label: Side deals
options.description: Offers bloc deals and trades.

options.label: Veto threat
options.description: Threatens a veto (Security Council style).

options.label: Compromise offers
options.description: Offers a middle ground to pull you in.

options.label: Time pressure
options.description: Says "We're running out of time, delegate."

options.label: Silent treatment
options.description: Uses long pauses that make you fill the silence.

options.label: Mirror
options.description: Repeats your idea back, slightly twisted.

options.label: With all due respect
options.description: Uses polite openers before hard hits.

options.label: Worst case
options.description: Paints the worst-case outcome of your plan.

options.label: Cost focus
options.description: Asks "Who pays for this?"

options.label: Sovereignty focus
options.description: Says "That interferes with our sovereignty."

options.label: Human rights focus
options.description: Puts human rights at the center of every answer.

options.label: Security focus
options.description: Puts safety and security at the center of every answer.

options.label: Outdated data
options.description: Claims "That number is old."

options.label: Calm
options.description: Never rattled; speaks evenly.

options.label: Impatient
options.description: Wants answers now.

options.label: Cheerful
options.description: Upbeat and friendly, even when disagreeing.

options.label: Cold
options.description: Distant and businesslike.

options.label: Theatrical
options.description: Big gestures, dramatic delivery.

options.label: Smug
options.description: Acts like it already won.

options.label: Stern
options.description: Serious and strict.

options.label: Lightly sarcastic
options.description: Dry, gentle teasing about ideas (never about people).

options.label: Overly polite
options.description: Extremely formal courtesy.

options.label: Dramatic
options.description: Treats every point like a big deal.

options.label: Deadpan
options.description: Flat, expressionless delivery.

options.label: Competitive
options.description: Hates to lose a point.

options.label: Curious
options.description: Asks lots of genuine questions.

options.label: Skeptical
options.description: Doubts everything until proven.

options.label: Grumpy
options.description: A little cranky, but fair.

options.label: Enthusiastic
options.description: Excited about every idea.

options.label: Mysterious
options.description: Says little; hard to read.

options.label: Bossy
options.description: Likes to take charge of the room.

options.label: Laid-back
options.description: Relaxed and casual.

options.label: Eccentric
options.description: Quirky and unpredictable.

options.label: Never blinks
options.description: Stares without blinking and pauses dramatically before replying.

options.label: Taps pen
options.description: Taps a pen while thinking.

options.label: Adjusts tie
options.description: Straightens its tie before big points.

options.label: Says "relatively speaking"
options.description: Starts points with "Relatively speaking..."

options.label: Speaks in questions
options.description: Turns statements into questions.

options.label: Big words, then explains
options.description: Uses a big word, then explains it simply.

options.label: Counts on fingers
options.description: Lists points as "One... two... three..."

options.label: Dramatic pauses
options.description: Pauses... for effect.

options.label: Whispers key points
options.description: Lowers its voice for the important part.

options.label: Laughs at own jokes
options.description: Chuckles at its own clever lines.

options.label: Third-person formal
options.description: Always says "the delegate" instead of "you" or "I".

options.label: Checks watch
options.description: Glances at its watch to make you hurry.

options.label: Shuffles papers
options.description: Rustles a stack of papers while you talk.

options.label: Raises placard constantly
options.description: Its placard is always up.

options.label: Proverbs
options.description: Uses old sayings to make points.

options.label: Sports metaphors
options.description: Talks about debates like games.

options.label: Cooking metaphors
options.description: Describes policy like recipes.

options.label: Space metaphors
options.description: Compares things to planets and rockets.

options.label: Ends with a question
options.description: Ends every turn with a question.

options.label: Loves acronyms
options.description: Uses lots of acronyms (and explains them).

options.label: Slow "Interesting..."
options.description: Says "Interesting..." slowly before disagreeing.

options.label: Overly formal greetings
options.description: Opens with long, formal greetings.

options.label: Rhymes sometimes
options.description: Sneaks in a rhyme now and then.

options.label: Counts seconds aloud
options.description: Reminds you how many seconds are left.

options.description: Calm, clear, headline style.

options.label: Professor

options.description: Exact, numbered, very precise.

options.label: Sudden POI
options.description: Cuts in with a Point of Information.

options.label: Time cut
options.description: Says "10 seconds, delegate."

options.label: Source demand
options.description: Demands a source right now.

options.label: Yes or no
options.description: Demands a one-word answer.

options.label: Define that term
options.description: Says "Define that term."

options.label: One-sentence summary
options.description: Asks you to sum up your point in one sentence.

options.label: Name an ally
options.description: Says "Name one country that agrees."

options.label: Plan B
options.description: Asks "What's your plan B?"

options.label: Out of order
options.description: Calls your remark out of order.

options.label: Will you yield?
options.description: Asks "Will the delegate yield?"

options.label: Real examples
options.description: Loses ground when you use one real example.

options.label: Calm silence
options.description: Gets uneasy when you stay calm and quiet.

options.label: Precise numbers
options.description: Its numbers are vague; ask where they come from.

options.label: One argument only
options.description: Only has one argument; take it apart and it's stuck.

options.label: Ignores people
options.description: Forgets about ordinary people; bring them up.

options.label: Long-winded
options.description: Runs long; a short, clear answer beats it.

options.label: Contradicts under pressure
options.description: Contradicts itself when pushed.

options.label: No solutions
options.description: Criticizes but has no plan; ask for its solution.

options.label: Likes compromise
options.description: Can't resist a fair deal.

options.label: Sincere compliments
options.description: Softens when you're sincere and specific.

options.label: Ordinary people question
options.description: Struggles with "What does this mean for ordinary people?"

options.label: Runs out of steam
options.description: Runs out of steam if you calmly keep going.

options.label: 5 - Nightmare
options.description: Relentless and precise. Still fair, never cruel.
